doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Being flexible and improvisation as life
summary: Jimmy refuses to name a favorite band and says life is improvisation.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Another level. And they all have their levels. That’s why I said to try to say which is my favorite, is very difficult for me, because they’re all very — for me anyway — very positive. I accept everything that went with it, because that’s what made it positive you see.
And that’s the only way you can hang out.
To be a musician you have to be, I think, super flexible. Because otherwise, how could you make it at all?

And also that coincides with, even though they coined that phrase “jazz” and they refer to “improvisation,” — the act of improving on something, right, improvisation, that’s what it is. That’s what I explain to my kids you see. I say everybody does that on this planet. Nobody knows everything. So living life is a total improvisational experience. And those who are trying to fix it so it’s like one-two-three, eventually find out it doesn’t work one- two-three all the time. They’ve got to deal with the law of permutation.
